2	"C01","The Hall(DC)+inductive-coil(AC) hybrid sensing architecture has direct prior art spanning 1999-2025: power electronics (HOKA probe), space magnetometry, fusion (JET RHP line and 2025 Kalman-fusion papers), and accelerator magnets.","observed","H055;H056;H003;H007;H008;H001;H002;H004;H059","strong_direct_multiple_domains","","Fusion-specific instances are concentrated in 2022-2025 within two overlapping author clusters (CERN/Arpaia; JET/Prague/KAERI).","20_observability;50_limitations_comparison;60_research_program;80_synthesis"
3	"C02","Correcting coil/integrator additive drift b_C with a non-integrating absolute reference (Hall, NMR, or magnet current) is hardware-proven (CERN bench: 59.9-120 ppm/s reduced to 0.02-0.08 ppm/s) and deployed at system level in ITER's outer-vessel steady-state sensor (OVSS) set.","observed","H004;H005;P003","strong_direct_hardware","","None of these estimate or correct Hall sensitivity S_H; P003 is metadata-verified only (content description not independently read).","20_observability;30_radiation_compensation;80_synthesis"
4	"C03","No verified peer-reviewed source jointly estimates {B, S_H, b_H, K_C, b_C} from a Hall+coil pair with a stated identifiability condition; the strongest identifiability proof found (rank condition for state+bias+unknown input) explicitly excludes an unknown sensor-gain term.","derived","H021;H012;H015;H016;H017","systematic_absence_after_documented_search","","Absence claim is bounded by the 10A search scope (7 domains); H021's own validation is simulation-only.","20_observability;60_research_program;70_redteam"
5	"C04","In absolute+rate two-sensor fusion, joint bias/state observability is excitation-conditional, not automatic (GPS/INS requires maneuvering; magnetometer bias determination degenerates in unfavorable geometry). Inference: Hall+coil mutual calibration will require persistent excitation or an injected known field; this condition is unproven for the Hall+coil pair specifically.","inferred","H018;H019;H020","strong_analog_theory","","GPS/INS and spacecraft-magnetometer analogs assume known absolute-sensor gain; the Hall case cannot.","20_observability;30_radiation_compensation"
6	"C05","JET RHP in-situ same-die microsolenoid AC self-test preserved InSb Hall sensitivity to SD ~0.07% over 11.5 years / >19,000 pulses including a D-T campaign; the same embedded microsolenoids double as inductive pickup coils.","observed","H003;H007","strong_direct_operational","","Same-technology, co-located reference: cannot by construction detect a common-mode (shared radiation/thermal) drift of die and reference coil together.","30_radiation_compensation;60_research_program;80_synthesis"
7	"C06","Existing Hall+coil drift correction does NOT prove in-situ Hall radiation-sensitivity calibration: every fusion-context instance corrects the coil/integrator chain using the Hall channel as reference and assumes S_H known or stable; no source demonstrates coil-derived identification of radiation-induced Hall gain or bias drift in any fusion or radiation environment.","derived","H001;H002;H004;H005;P003","systematic_absence_after_documented_search","H059","H059 (counterevidence only in direction, not environment) shows in-situ coil-calibrates-Hall in a non-fusion HTS magnet under a driven, known ramp with no radiation exposure.","20_observability;30_radiation_compensation;40_applications_collaboration;50_limitations_comparison;60_research_program;70_redteam;80_synthesis"

9	"C08","Embedded known-field calibration references exist at chip scale (on-chip reference actuator next to a Hall array, ~392 mT/A per coil) and machine scale (HBT-EP 'artificial plasma' calibration coils used to calibrate 216 Mirnov coils and a Rogowski coil in situ).","observed","H038;H040","moderate_direct","","H038's quantitative figures are search-snippet-sourced (flagged for full-text read); H040 calibrates inductive sensors, not a Hall channel.","30_radiation_compensation;60_research_program"

11	"C10","In superconducting-magnet quench detection, Hall-array and coil (quench-antenna) approaches remain parallel, unfused research lines even in well-resourced programs - a counter-signal against assuming Hall+coil fusion is trivial engineering.","observed","H060;H061","moderate_direct","","Two sources, one sub-domain; absence of fusion there does not prove difficulty, only non-adoption.","50_limitations_comparison;70_redteam"
12	"C11","The reverse correction direction - coil channel calibrating the Hall channel in situ - is abstract-confirmed in exactly one non-fusion case: the Feather-M2 HTS dipole's cryogenic Hall sensors were cross-calibrated in situ against induction-coil sensors during driven magnet ramps.","observed","H059","single_source_direct","","Non-fusion, no radiation, engineered excitation (known dB/dt from a driven ramp); quantitative accuracy figures not read (abstract-level access).","20_observability;30_radiation_compensation;60_research_program"

16	"C15","AlGaN/GaN 2DEG proton damage is quantified (2 MeV, 6e14 cm-2: mobility -28.9%, 2DEG density -12.1%, interface broadened 2.2 nm); AlGaN/GaN micro-Hall sensors are only slightly affected at ~1e13 p/cm2 with degradation rising at higher fluence and PARTIAL recovery on annealing.","observed","R022;R012;R013;R015","moderate_direct","","R012/R013/R015 quantitative conditions are secondary-sourced (publisher blocked); R022 figures are Crossref-abstract-confirmed.","30_radiation_compensation"
17	"C16","NIEL-based proton-to-gamma damage scaling under-predicts Co-60 gamma lifetime damage by ~14x in InAs/InAsSb, because proton cascade defects self-anneal more efficiently than gamma-produced isolated Frenkel pairs. Cross-species extrapolation is unsafe for III-V Hall materials.","observed","R042","single_source_direct","","One material family (InAs/InAsSb infrared detectors), minority-carrier-lifetime metric - mechanism argument transfers to Hall parameters only as a labeled inference.","30_radiation_compensation;70_redteam"
18	"C17","Mixed neutron+gamma damage is non-additive, and the direction of the non-additivity depends on device structure and the electrical quantity examined (GaN HEMT leakage sub-additive vs cascode threshold super-additive; bipolar op-amp offset synergistic).","observed","R028;R046","moderate_direct","","Two device classes only; no Hall-device combined-field dataset exists (see C14/C21).","30_radiation_compensation;70_redteam"
19	"C18","A metallic (copper-active-layer) Hall sensor on ceramic substrate showed no measurable sensitivity change up to ~1e18 n/cm2 fission-spectrum fluence, with sensitivity flat over 100-250 C. Inference: metallic Hall is a candidate material-diverse reference channel for a semiconductor Hall+coil system.","inferred","R071","single_source_direct","","Single source, abstract-level access, single fluence/temperature envelope; the inference (use as reference channel) is this mission's, not the paper's.","30_radiation_compensation;60_research_program"
20	"C19","Radiation-induced EMF (RIEMF) in mineral-insulated cables is an established additive error mechanism for coil signal chains (five-paper cluster, 1997-2004; ITER aims to keep non-inductive voltage well below 1 uV for 3000-s pulses per secondary-sourced figures).","observed","R056;R057;R058;R059;R060","strong_direct_multiple_sources","","No dose-to-RIEMF-magnitude curve could be independently confirmed (publisher access blocked); the 1 uV figure is secondary-sourced.","30_radiation_compensation"
21	"C20","The JET fibre-optic current sensor (FOCS) operated through the DTE2 D-T campaign (~8.5e20 total neutrons): Verdet constant +/-4% shot-to-shot, a possible ~0.7% campaign-scale drift at low statistical confidence, no disqualifying degradation, continuously cross-validated against the Continuous External Rogowski - the only in-machine D-T radiation-effects dataset in the ledger, and a template for what Hall+coil qualification would need to produce.","observed","R063;H031;R064;R065","strong_direct_fulltext","","FOCS is a Faraday-effect optical sensor, not a Hall device; transfer of its qualification template to Hall+coil is a proposal, not evidence.","30_radiation_compensation;40_applications_collaboration;60_research_program"
22	"C21","In-situ (during-irradiation) recalibration of Hall sensitivity against a material-diverse reference is unreported for any Hall material, in any source found by either the radiation or hybrid lane.","unknown","R001;R002;R003;R012;R013;R071;H003;H007","systematic_absence_after_documented_search","","Bounded by 10A+10B search scope; JET RHP self-test (C05) is same-die, not material-diverse.","20_observability;30_radiation_compensation;60_research_program;70_redteam"
23	"C22","GaN-family TID response has two regimes: a rapidly-annealing low-dose threshold shift (<3 krad(SiO2)) common to HEMT and MOS-HEMT, and a persistent oxide-trapping shift extending to at least 2 Mrad in MOS-HEMTs only; a 200 C / 25 min anneal partially recovers gamma-degraded transport.","observed","R024;R033","moderate_direct","","R024 uses 10 keV X-rays as TID surrogate (not gamma); R033 is peer_review_uncertain (ECS Transactions proceedings).","30_radiation_compensation"
24	"C23","Heavily irradiated III-V material converges toward a material-specific limiting Fermi level (InAs to n+-type, InSb to p-type, under 5-10 MeV protons at 2e16 cm-2), consistent with Fermi-level-stabilization theory. Inference: radiation-induced InSb/InAs Hall parameter drift may asymptote (bounded) rather than diverge - a falsifiable model input, unconfirmed under neutron exposure.","inferred","R036;R037;R038","mechanism_based_inference","R042","Proton-only evidence; R042 warns cross-species scaling within III-Vs can err by an order of magnitude, so the neutron-case asymptote must be tested, not assumed.","30_radiation_compensation;60_research_program"
25	"C24","Transmutation is a permanent (non-annealable at service temperatures) damage channel: thermal-neutron Ga-to-Ge conversion in GaN required a 950 C activation anneal; In/Sb thermal-neutron capture is the attributed driver of InSb fission-spectrum sensitivity loss.","observed","R025;R001;R002","moderate_direct","","R025 is a doping demonstration on bulk GaN, not a sensor-degradation study; the permanence-in-service conclusion is a labeled inference from the 950 C figure.","30_radiation_compensation"
26	"C25","Readout-chain radiation failure modes are distinct from sensor-die damage and must be budgeted separately: bipolar op-amp offset/bias-current degradation with neutron+gamma synergy; millisecond-scale single-event transients originating in op-amp bias/startup circuitry; COTS ADC TID/SEU evaluation exists as methodology; the only 1-MGy-class rad-hard instrumentation-amplifier design found is simulation-only.","observed","R046;R052;R051;R050;R047;R055","moderate_direct","","Most quantitative thresholds are secondary-sourced or unread (publisher access); R050 must never be cited as experimental validation.","30_radiation_compensation;50_limitations_comparison"
27	"C26","Activation-foil dosimetry is a mature, validated fluence-monitoring practice: VERDI detectors benchmarked at a 14 MeV D-T reference field (C/E = 1.05 +/- 0.13) and then validated in-machine at JET D-D to 8% agreement; the two-step protocol (reference-field calibration, then in-machine validation) is the model for any Hall irradiation campaign's dosimetry.","observed","R076;R075;R072;R073;R074;R078","strong_direct_multiple_sources","","Foil dosimetry gives fluence/spectrum, not sensor-parameter drift; surrogate-facility flux can sit 3-5 orders of magnitude below the target environment (R074).","30_radiation_compensation;60_research_program"
28	"C27","ITER's OVSS is the strongest real-machine precedent for the DC-Hall-corrects-coil-drift half of the proposed hybrid; it is a system-level pairing of separate sensor heads with downstream fusion, not a co-located single-package hybrid, and the reverse direction (coil identifies Hall drift) is untested on any tokamak.","observed","P003","single_source_direct","H059","P003 content description is metadata-verified only; H059 demonstrates the reverse direction only in a non-fusion HTS magnet.","40_applications_collaboration;60_research_program;80_synthesis"
29	"C28","Persistent-mode superconducting/HTS magnets are a documented poor fit: a coil is structurally blind to a static trapped field (no dB/dt after magnetization), and the field's accepted precision reference for that state is NMR, not a coil (persistent-mode NMR magnet held >2 years at ~3e-5 ppm/h drift with NMR cross-check).","observed","P042;P038;P040;P041;P045","strong_direct_fulltext","P039;P049","Counterevidence limited to the brief magnetization transient itself, where pickup coils and Hall arrays are both used (P039, P049).","40_applications_collaboration;50_limitations_comparison"
30	"C29","Accelerator-magnet metrology already combines Hall probes + rotating/fixed coils + NMR as decades-old production practice, including in-situ calibration of rotating coils against a reference magnet - direct prior art that vetoes any architecture-level novelty claim in that domain.","observed","P052;P054;P057;P058;P055;P056;P075","strong_direct_multiple_sources","","Bench/test-stand context without fusion-grade radiation; the radiation/in-situ-embedded angle remains open (C36).","40_applications_collaboration;50_limitations_comparison;70_redteam"
31	"C30","Z-pinch/pulsed-power practice solved its redundancy need by cross-calibrating and fusing two inductive sensors (B-dot + Rogowski, +/-13-15%), deliberately bypassing Hall sensors; Hall-effect current sensors are independently documented as EMI-susceptible (tangential RF E-field) in power-electronics testing.","observed","P025;P028;P022;P021","moderate_direct","","The EMI-susceptibility-to-z-pinch transfer is an explicit inference (power-electronics test conditions, not a z-pinch measurement); ns-us timescales leave no DC baseline for a Hall channel to anchor.","40_applications_collaboration;50_limitations_comparison"
32	"C31","Magnetoresistive alternatives compete directly on the DC+broadband axis: TMR sensors span DC-to-broadband in one channel and showed no key-parameter degradation to 5 Mrad(Si) gamma/X-ray under bias; AMR tolerated 200 krad(Si) gamma with the front-end electronics as the weaker element.","observed","P064;P063;P062","moderate_direct","","Gamma/X-ray only - no neutron displacement-damage evidence for TMR/AMR was found; P063 was upgraded to verified at 10D after its author list was resolved.","40_applications_collaboration;50_limitations_comparison;70_redteam"
33	"C32","Stellarator field verification relies on electron-beam flux-surface mapping during commissioning (vacuum only, cannot coexist with plasma) plus trim-coil correction informed by it; no literature exists on a Hall+coil hybrid for stellarator field mapping.","observed","P013;P018;P019;P020;P012;P014;P016","systematic_absence_after_documented_search","","The absence cuts both ways: an open niche for the user's HSX context, but zero prior validation to build on.","40_applications_collaboration;60_research_program"
34	"C33","Long-pulse/steady-state magnetic diagnostics need non-inductive DC sensing as a design requirement, not a preference: DEMO's antimony-Hall steady-state program states inductive sensors 'require supplementation'; DEMO-class printed coils are qualified to >=500 C; WEST rebuilt its 469-sensor suite for ~1000-s pulses.","observed","H065;P009;P004;P006;P010","strong_direct_multiple_sources","","JT-60SA's 200 C / 9 MGy in-vessel figures (P006) are secondary-sourced and unconfirmed at full text.","40_applications_collaboration;60_research_program"
35	"C34","Fibre-optic (Faraday) current sensing is a credible competing upgrade path for tokamak current measurement (ITER FOCS accuracy limited by Faraday-mirror imperfections with a published compensation route; T-15MD concept; JET DTE2 validation) - EMI-immune, integrator-free, DC-capable.","observed","P066;P067;R063;H029;H030","strong_direct_multiple_sources","","FOCS measures enclosed current, not local field - it competes with Rogowski/current diagnostics, not with local field mapping.","40_applications_collaboration;50_limitations_comparison"
36	"C35","Where the environment already forced practitioners to abandon magnetic probes entirely (MagLIF load region uses optical PDV for peak current; hot dense pinch column uses spectroscopic Zeeman splitting), a Hall+coil hybrid adds no survivability and is out of scope.","observed","P031;P032","moderate_direct","","Two sub-domains; the boundary is physical survivability, not sensing principle.","40_applications_collaboration;50_limitations_comparison"
37	"C36","Novelty constraints after direct prior-art analysis: architecture-level 'Hall+coil hybrid' is NOT novel (C01, C29); the credible remaining gaps are (a) a joint gain+bias+state identifiability proof for the Hall+coil pair, (b) hardware-validated bidirectional mutual correction in a real plasma and/or radiation environment, (c) in-situ radiation-aware Hall recalibration against a material-diverse reference, and (d) the stellarator-mapping application niche.","derived","H021;H001;H002;H004;H059;P003;P052;P057;R071;P013","synthesis_of_documented_gaps","","Each gap is an absence claim bounded by this mission's search scope; a dedicated prior-art search should precede any publication claim on gaps (a)-(d).","60_research_program;70_redteam;80_synthesis"
38	"C37","Sequencing: validating the Hall channel first, then hybridizing, remains a defensible engineering order (a working calibrated Hall channel is a prerequisite for any fused system), but hybridization itself must not be the headline novelty claim; the contribution should target the C36 gaps.","proposed","H001;H002;H003;H004;H021","proposal_from_documented_premises","","Scope decision belongs to the user/advisor; this stage records the evidence-side constraints only.","60_research_program;80_synthesis"

14	   pairs, clusters, carrier removal, mobility loss, deep traps in the
15	   semiconductor bulk [R035, R040, R022, R026, R027].

17	   insulators, packaging, and analog electronics [R024, R044, R045, R047].
18	3. **Transmutation** (thermal-neutron capture): permanent element conversion
19	   ΓÇö GaΓåÆGe in GaN [R025]; In/Sb capture products in InSb [R001] (C24).
20	
21	## 2. Direct Hall-device evidence, material ├ù species (Observed)
22	
23	- **InSb** (the material fielded at JET/ITER): sensitivity drops under a
24	  *thermal-inclusive fission* spectrum at ~1e16 n/cm┬▓ yet is stable under a
25	  *purely fast* spectrum at comparable fluence ΓÇö attributed by the authors to
26	  transmutation, not displacement (R001, R002) (C12). At 6.6ΓÇô7.0e17 fast
27	  n/cm┬▓ (~200 ┬░C), thin-film InSb mobility fell 75ΓÇô90 % (avg 83 %, 9
28	  samples), carrier-density direction doping-dependent (R003, full text)
29	  (C13). Consequence (Derived): an integrated-fluence number without spectral
30	  shape is not a sufficient predictor of InSb Hall drift.
31	- **GaAs**: conductivity and Hall mobility fall over 1e13ΓÇô3e15 n/cm┬▓ with an
32	  n/p-inversion signature at the top of that range (R043); Co-60 gamma shows
33	  a low-dose stabilizing / high-dose degrading split near (8ΓÇô10)e3 Gy (R009,
34	  R010); gamma/beta comparison ranks Si/Ge as more tolerant than InSb/GaAs
35	  via displacement-threshold arguments (R008).
36	- **Si/SOI**: direct evidence is bulk/detector-grade characterization (R007,
37	  R020, R021, R040), not packaged sensors; the FD-SOI Hall "radiation
38	  effects" paper is **TCAD simulation only** (R044 ΓÇö seed-list error
39	  documented; simulated TID *raised* sensitivity +29 %) and must never be
40	  cited as experiment.

42	  neutron irradiation exists in the peer-reviewed literature ΓÇö any
43	  spectrum** (C14, Unknown/gap). The closest direct devices are AlGaN/GaN
44	  *micro-Hall sensors under protons*: only slightly affected at ~1e13 p/cm┬▓,
45	  degrading toward 1e16, with **partial** anneal recovery and a cryogenic
46	  sensitivity-enhancement anomaly (R012ΓÇôR016; quantitative details

48	  protons at 6e14 cmΓü╗┬▓ cut mobility 28.9 % and 2DEG density 12.1 % (R022,
49	  abstract-confirmed) (C15).

51	  ~1e18 n/cm┬▓, flat 100ΓÇô250 ┬░C (R071, single source) (C18).
52	- **Packaged Hall ICs**: TID tolerance 40ΓÇô100 krad(Si) class, SEE-hard to
53	  LET 67.7 MeV┬╖cm┬▓/mg in one part, TID-induced errors partly anneal-
54	  recoverable (R011, R018, R019).

56	## 3. Cross-species and combined-field warnings (Observed; counterevidence)

58	1. **NIEL scaling fails across species within one material family:** Co-60
59	   gamma lifetime damage in InAs/InAsSb is ~14├ù the proton-scaled prediction
60	   ΓÇö proton cascade defects self-anneal; gamma's isolated Frenkel pairs do
61	   not (R042) (C16). Any proton-test-based projection of gamma (or neutron)
62	   response for a III-V Hall die is unsafe without a mechanism argument.

64	   neutron + Co-60 gamma in GaN HEMTs gives sub-additive leakage but
65	   super-additive threshold shift in the cascode structure (R028); mixed
66	   neutron+gamma in a bipolar OP07 is synergistic (R046) (C17). Single-
67	   species Hall data cannot be summed to predict a fusion mixed field.

69	   irradiated InAs/InSb converge to material-specific limiting Fermi levels

71	   parameter drift. Proton-only; unconfirmed under neutrons, and C16 warns
72	   against silent transfer (C23).
73	
74	## 4. Measurement chain (kept separate from sensor-die physics)
75	
76	- **Electronics** (C25): bipolar op-amp offset/bias degradation with mixed-
77	  field synergy (R046); ELDRS-type dose-rate/temperature sensitivity (R047);
78	  millisecond-scale single-event transients from op-amp bias/startup
79	  circuitry (R052) ΓÇö a transient corruption mode distinct from slow TID

81	  rad-hard instrumentation amplifier found is **simulation-only** (R050).
82	  Current-sense-amplifier TID work exists but content is unverified (R055).
83	- **Coil chain** (C19): RIEMF in mineral-insulated cable is established by a
84	  five-paper cluster (R056ΓÇôR060; theory R059 vs experiment R060 kept
85	  distinct), with a secondary-sourced ITER target of Γë¬1 ┬╡V non-inductive
86	  voltage for 3000-s pulses; a separate radiation+thermal-gradient
87	  core-to-sheath asymmetry is *uncorrelated* with core-to-core RIEMF (R048),
88	  and copper-core activation (Γü╢Γü╢Cu beta decay) is a named, avoidable
89	  mechanism ΓÇö steel core sidesteps it (R049). Insulation: matched
90	  cryogenic organic-vs-ceramic pair (Kapton R061 vs alumina R062); FRP
91	  interlaminar shear at 4 K (R068). JET's in-vessel Mirnov coils suffered

98	  DTE2 (~8.5e20 D-T neutrons; ~1.5e12 n/cm┬▓/s peak at the sensor), Verdet
99	  constant ┬▒4 % shot-to-shot, a possible ~0.7 % campaign drift at low
100	  statistical confidence, no disqualifying degradation, continuously
101	  cross-validated against the CER Rogowski (R063 full text; pre-campaign
102	  baseline H031; gamma-only Verdet study R064; in-pulse fiber attenuation
103	  R065).

105	  verified source (R067, space context) ΓÇö the thinnest sub-topic in the
106	  ledger (gap).
107	
108	## 5. Dosimetry and qualification practice (Observed, C26)
109	
110	Activation-foil dosimetry is mature and validated: VERDI benchmarked at the
111	14 MeV FNG reference field (C/E = 1.05 ┬▒ 0.13, R076), then validated
112	in-machine at JET D-D to 8 % (R075); protocol formalized as reference-field
113	calibration ΓåÆ in-machine validation (R072); TU Dresden's ITER-TBM
114	foil-activation program explicitly quantifies the surrogate-facility gap ΓÇö
115	its test flux sits 3ΓÇô5 orders of magnitude below full-power ITER-TBM flux
116	(R073, R074). KSTAR runs a routine activation system (R078). **Derived:** any
117	Hall irradiation campaign inherits a ready-made dosimetry protocol; the
118	surrogate-to-target flux gap and the spectral-shape sensitivity (C12) must
119	both be stated in its design.

122

124

126	  oxide-trapping) offset/threshold behavior for GaN-family electronics
127	  (R024, R033) (C22); RIEMF as an additive coil-chain term of established
128	  existence but unquantified dose curve (C19); the bounded-asymptote
129	  hypothesis for III-V parameters (C23, Inferred only).
130	- **Monitorable now:** fluence/spectrum via activation foils (C26);
131	  temperature as a first-class state (tracked explicitly in R003, R022,
132	  R037, R038, R071).
133	- **Calibratable in principle, undemonstrated in practice:**
134	  **no source in either lane demonstrates in-situ, during-irradiation
135	  recalibration of Hall sensitivity against a material-diverse reference,
136	  for any Hall material (C21, Unknown).** The fielded JET solution (H003/
137	  H007) is same-die self-test ΓÇö vulnerable, by construction, to common-mode
138	  radiation/thermal drift of die and reference together.
139	- **Required statement (Derived, C06):** the existence of Hall+coil (and
140	  HallΓåÆcoil) drift-correction architectures does **not** prove that
141	  radiation-induced Hall sensitivity drift can be calibrated in situ. The
142	  demonstrated direction of correction is coil-drift-from-Hall-reference;
143	  the radiation problem needs the opposite direction (or an independent
144	  reference), whose observability is unproven (hybrid review ┬º3ΓÇô4).
145	- **Candidate architecture elements the evidence supports (Inferred/
146	  Proposed):** a metallic-Hall witness channel (R071's null result ΓÇö single
147	  source, needs replication), an embedded known-field injection winding
148	  (H038/H007 lineage), activation-foil dosimetry co-located with the sensor
149	  (C26), and explicit temperature telemetry. These are design inputs for
150	  stage 30, not conclusions.
151	
152	## 7. Gaps (Unknown; carried to stages 30/60/70)
153	
154	1. Bare GaN/AlGaN Hall-plate neutron response ΓÇö none exists (C14).
155	2. 14 MeV D-T direct Hall data ΓÇö none; FOCS is the only in-machine D-T
156	   dataset and is not a Hall device (C20).
157	3. Combined neutron+gamma+temperature Hall dataset ΓÇö none; non-additivity
158	   demonstrated only in HEMTs/op-amps (C17).
159	4. In-situ material-diverse Hall recalibration ΓÇö unreported (C21).
160	5. Dose-to-RIEMF and dose-to-effective-area curves ΓÇö unquantified (C19).
161	6. Integrator/timing-chain radiation data ΓÇö single space-context source
162	   (R067).

## 5. Embedded calibration winding ΓÇö required analysis

**The stage question: can the winding's field isolate Hall gain and bias
in the presence of an unknown ambient field?**

### 5.1 What injection can and cannot isolate (Derived; CASE E)

With `B_inj(t) = G_cal┬╖I_cal(t)` spectrally orthogonal to ambient
content:

- **Gain: yes, as a product.** Lock-in demodulation of `y_H` at the
  injection frequency estimates `S_H┬╖G_cal` (CASE E, rank 6/7 ΓÇö both
  gain functions identifiable). Relative gain tracking
  `[S_H┬╖G_cal](t) / [S_H┬╖G_cal](t_0)` is the radiation-monitoring
  quantity of interest and is insensitive to the ambient field entirely.
- **Bias: no ΓÇö structurally.** The DC null survives every AC injection
  (CASE E): a Hall offset is observationally identical to a static
  ambient shift. Toggled DC injection (`┬▒I_cal,DC`, difference of
  states) measures *gain at the DC operating point* ΓÇö the difference
  `╬öy_H = 2┬╖S_H┬╖G_cal┬╖I_cal,DC` cancels both `b_H` and static ambient ΓÇö
  but never `b_H` itself. Offset requires zero-field/known-field epochs
  (MVD anchor ii) or an absolute reference. **Any design document
  claiming an embedded winding "calibrates the offset" is wrong**
  (Derived, Theorem 1 ╬▓-direction).
- Ambient variation *during* a toggle period leaks into the toggle
  difference; mitigation is fast square-wave toggling with synchronous
  demod, with the main coil as a dB/dt witness to gate/correct toggle
  epochs (Derived).

### 5.2 Frequency plan and lock-in detection (Derived design rules)

- Place `f_inj` in the **overlap band**: above the drift band `╧ë_d`,
  below the Hall pole, inside the coil's flat response ΓÇö
  `╧ë_d < 2╧Ç┬╖f_inj < min(a_Hall, ╧ë_C,max)` ΓÇö and in a measured-quiet
  region of the ambient spectrum. Spectral collision with ambient
  content re-creates the rank deficiency (CASE E-collide: 5/7) ΓÇö this is
  a hard requirement, not a preference. Machine EMI lines (power
  supplies, spinning-current harmonics) must be surveyed first
  (Hall-sensor EMI susceptibility is documented in adjacent contexts,
  [P021], [P022], C30).
- Coding (PRBS or slow frequency hopping) or on/off toggling makes the
  orthogonality verifiable: the estimator checks that the demodulated
  output tracks the injection schedule (loss-of-injection and
  collision-detection test in fault bank S4).
- Lock-in variance (first-order, matched-filter): for a sine injection
  of amplitude `B_a = G_cal┬╖I_a`,
  `var(┼£_H┬╖G_cal) Γëê 2╧â_H┬▓ / (T_int ┬╖ I_a┬▓┬╖G_cal┬▓)` ΓÇö integration time
  `T_int` trades against the drift timescale being tracked
  (quasi-stationarity window, stage-20 assumption 3). Choose `T_int` Γë¬
  expected drift correlation time; since GaN drift magnitudes are
  Unknown (C14), `T_int` is a *scheduled parameter*, revisited after
  validation rung 5 data exists.
- Coil-side lock-in: the coil sees `d(B_inj)/dt`, amplitude
  `Γê¥ ╧ë_inj┬╖B_a`, so coil-side SNR *improves* with frequency ΓÇö favoring
  the upper part of the allowed band, jointly optimized against the Hall
  pole margin (case 9: injecting near the pole additionally identifies
  Hall dynamics; CASE H-broad).

### 5.3 Amplitude, heating, EMI (Derived design constraints)

- **Amplitude floor:** `B_a` must give usable lock-in SNR within `T_int`
  (formula above) at the Hall noise floor.
- **Heating ceiling (self-interference):** winding dissipation
  `P_cal = I_rms┬▓┬╖R_cal` raises die temperature by `╬öT_die = R_th┬╖P_cal`,
  which enters the very term (`╬▒_S┬╖╬öT`) the system is trying to
  monitor. Self-consistency condition:
  `|╬▒_S| ┬╖ R_th ┬╖ R_cal ┬╖ I_rms┬▓ Γë¬ ╬┤_S` (target relative-gain
  resolution). This couples winding resistance, thermal design, and
  amplitude; it is a bench-characterizable inequality (Tier 1), and a
  reason the winding cannot simply be driven harder to buy SNR.
- **EMI/coupling:** the injection tone couples into the main coil by
  mutual inductance ΓÇö this is *used* (┬º5.5), but also contaminates the
  coil's field measurement at `f_inj`; the demodulator must notch the
  injection line out of the field-estimation path. Injection leads must
  be twisted/guarded so the *cable*, not just the winding, does not
  radiate (RIEMF and pickup discipline as for the main coil, C19).
- Under radiation, the cal circuit itself is exposed: RIEMF adds an
  error current/EMF in the injection loop ([R056] mechanism; Inferred
  transfer ΓÇö flagged, risk RR-12), and insulation leakage changes the
  delivered `I_cal` unless the readback shunt sits electrically close to
  the winding (design rule: **sense at the winding, not at the source**).

### 5.4 The winding's own reference problem (stage-required; Derived)

`G_cal` is geometry + magnetics. The stage forbids assuming it stays
known, and the evidence supports the caution: **no measurement of
radiation-induced coil-constant/effective-area drift exists for any
coil** (radiation review ┬º4 gap; metrology baseline [R069], [R070]), and
thermal expansion alone changes `G_cal` at the `╬▒_thermal┬╖╬öT` level.
Consequences:

1. Only the **products** `S_H┬╖G_cal`, `K_C┬╖G_cal` are identifiable
   (CASE E). A reference-chain drift is indistinguishable from sensor
   gain drift *within the winding system alone*.
2. The JET RHP record shows the strength and the limit of the same-die
   approach: 11.5 years, SD Γëê 0.07 % sensitivity stability across
   >19,000 pulses including D-T ([H003], [H007], C05) ΓÇö but a co-located
   same-technology reference cannot by construction detect common-mode
   (shared radiation/thermal) drift of die and winding together (C05
   limitation). Mechanism diversity (geometric constant vs semiconductor
   transport) makes common-mode drift *physically unlikely* but not
   logically excluded (Inferred, stage-20 ┬º5.5).
3. **Resolution in this architecture: triangulation, not trust.** The
   winding is itself referenced against the machine-model anchor at
   every vacuum-shot epoch (CASE D identifies `S_H` and `K_C`
   absolutely; combined with the lock-in products this *solves for
   `G_cal` at each anchor epoch* ΓÇö Derived). Between anchors, `G_cal`
   drift is bounded by the closure test below, and its residual drift
   rate enters the uncertainty budget explicitly (┬º6.3) rather than
   being assumed zero.

### 5.5 Triangle-closure consistency test (Derived; added design feature)

The three continuously-available quantities

```text
╧ü_HC   = S_H/K_C            (ambient AC cross-regression, CASE A invariant)
╧Ç_H    = S_H┬╖G_cal          (Hall-side lock-in)
╧Ç_C    = K_C┬╖G_cal          (coil-side lock-in)
```

satisfy the identity `╧Ç_H / ╧Ç_C Γëí ╧ü_HC` for all t. The **closure
residual** `╬╡_╬ö = ╧Ç_H/╧Ç_C ΓêÆ ╧ü_HC` is measurable continuously and must be
zero to within noise regardless of drift in any single quantity.
`╬╡_╬ö Γëá 0` indicts the *measurement paths* (demodulator fault, spectral
collision, coil nonlinearity at `f_inj`, injection-line contamination) ΓÇö
a fault-detection channel that costs nothing extra. Note what it cannot
do: closure holds identically under any {`S_H`, `K_C`, `G_cal`} drift,
so it provides **no drift attribution** ΓÇö it validates the
instrumentation, not the calibration (consistent with Theorem 1; no
free lunch).

### 6.1 Estimator states and structure

**Proposed** (structure per stage-20 estimator-requirements rows;
augmented-bias-state precedent [H015], [H004]):

- **Core filter (always on):** states

- **Gain-tracking layer (HA):** lock-in outputs `╧Ç_H, ╧Ç_C` as auxiliary
  measurements updating slowly-varying multiplicative states

  as direct (noisy) observations of the relative gains, valid under the
  ┬º5.2 orthogonality condition.
- **Anchor-epoch processors (scheduled):** vacuum-shot least squares on
  `[B_ref, 1]` and `[ß╕é_ref, 1]` (CASE D); zero-field offset reads

  writes `{┼£_H, K╠é_C, b╠é_H, b╠é_C, ─£_cal, cov}` to the calibration ledger
  (S5) with full uncertainty.
- **Fault bank (always on):** ╧ü-jump alarm; triangle-closure residual;
  innovation ╧ç┬▓; GLR change-point tests on gain states;
  loss-of-injection detector; (top tier) three-channel voting per

  *heuristic prior* for failure-vs-drift sorting, never as proof
  (stage-20 confounding row 6).

  non-identifiability (CASE A between anchors, CASE F quasi-static
  without injection), the estimator must **freeze** the corresponding
  states and inflate reported uncertainty, not "converge" on its prior

  simulation plan (test T-NI).

| **Online compensation** | core KF (integrator drift, offsets vs anchors); lock-in gain tracking; ╧ü-alarm-gated deweighting | continuous | `x_I, m, ╧ä_L, b_C`; relative `S_H, K_C` (HA); field estimate fusion | C02 direction (CASE C2/I); CASE E products; CASE A invariant |

2. **Between-anchor drift:** random-walk growth of frozen states ΓÇö

3. **Gain-tracking noise:** lock-in variance (┬º5.2 formula) plus `G_cal`

## 5. Embedded calibration winding ΓÇö required analysis

**The stage question: can the winding's field isolate Hall gain and bias
in the presence of an unknown ambient field?**

### 5.1 What injection can and cannot isolate (Derived; CASE E)

With `B_inj(t) = G_cal┬╖I_cal(t)` spectrally orthogonal to ambient
content:

- **Gain: yes, as a product.** Lock-in demodulation of `y_H` at the
  injection frequency estimates `S_H┬╖G_cal` (CASE E, rank 6/7 ΓÇö both
  gain functions identifiable). Relative gain tracking
  `[S_H┬╖G_cal](t) / [S_H┬╖G_cal](t_0)` is the radiation-monitoring
  quantity of interest and is insensitive to the ambient field entirely.
- **Bias: no ΓÇö structurally.** The DC null survives every AC injection
  (CASE E): a Hall offset is observationally identical to a static
  ambient shift. Toggled DC injection (`┬▒I_cal,DC`, difference of
  states) measures *gain at the DC operating point* ΓÇö the difference
  `╬öy_H = 2┬╖S_H┬╖G_cal┬╖I_cal,DC` cancels both `b_H` and static ambient ΓÇö
  but never `b_H` itself. Offset requires zero-field/known-field epochs
  (MVD anchor ii) or an absolute reference. **Any design document
  claiming an embedded winding "calibrates the offset" is wrong**
  (Derived, Theorem 1 ╬▓-direction).
- Ambient variation *during* a toggle period leaks into the toggle
  difference; mitigation is fast square-wave toggling with synchronous
  demod, with the main coil as a dB/dt witness to gate/correct toggle
  epochs (Derived).

### 5.2 Frequency plan and lock-in detection (Derived design rules)

- Place `f_inj` in the **overlap band**: above the drift band `╧ë_d`,
  below the Hall pole, inside the coil's flat response ΓÇö
  `╧ë_d < 2╧Ç┬╖f_inj < min(a_Hall, ╧ë_C,max)` ΓÇö and in a measured-quiet
  region of the ambient spectrum. Spectral collision with ambient
  content re-creates the rank deficiency (CASE E-collide: 5/7) ΓÇö this is
  a hard requirement, not a preference. Machine EMI lines (power
  supplies, spinning-current harmonics) must be surveyed first
  (Hall-sensor EMI susceptibility is documented in adjacent contexts,
  [P021], [P022], C30).
- Coding (PRBS or slow frequency hopping) or on/off toggling makes the
  orthogonality verifiable: the estimator checks that the demodulated
  output tracks the injection schedule (loss-of-injection and
  collision-detection test in fault bank S4).
- Lock-in variance (first-order, matched-filter): for a sine injection
  of amplitude `B_a = G_cal┬╖I_a`,
  `var(┼£_H┬╖G_cal) Γëê 2╧â_H┬▓ / (T_int ┬╖ I_a┬▓┬╖G_cal┬▓)` ΓÇö integration time
  `T_int` trades against the drift timescale being tracked
  (quasi-stationarity window, stage-20 assumption 3). Choose `T_int` Γë¬
  expected drift correlation time; since GaN drift magnitudes are
  Unknown (C14), `T_int` is a *scheduled parameter*, revisited after
  validation rung 5 data exists.
- Coil-side lock-in: the coil sees `d(B_inj)/dt`, amplitude
  `Γê¥ ╧ë_inj┬╖B_a`, so coil-side SNR *improves* with frequency ΓÇö favoring
  the upper part of the allowed band, jointly optimized against the Hall
  pole margin (case 9: injecting near the pole additionally identifies
  Hall dynamics; CASE H-broad).

### 5.3 Amplitude, heating, EMI (Derived design constraints)

- **Amplitude floor:** `B_a` must give usable lock-in SNR within `T_int`
  (formula above) at the Hall noise floor.
- **Heating ceiling (self-interference):** winding dissipation
  `P_cal = I_rms┬▓┬╖R_cal` raises die temperature by `╬öT_die = R_th┬╖P_cal`,
  which enters the very term (`╬▒_S┬╖╬öT`) the system is trying to
  monitor. Self-consistency condition:
  `|╬▒_S| ┬╖ R_th ┬╖ R_cal ┬╖ I_rms┬▓ Γë¬ ╬┤_S` (target relative-gain
  resolution). This couples winding resistance, thermal design, and
  amplitude; it is a bench-characterizable inequality (Tier 1), and a
  reason the winding cannot simply be driven harder to buy SNR.
- **EMI/coupling:** the injection tone couples into the main coil by
  mutual inductance ΓÇö this is *used* (┬º5.5), but also contaminates the
  coil's field measurement at `f_inj`; the demodulator must notch the
  injection line out of the field-estimation path. Injection leads must
  be twisted/guarded so the *cable*, not just the winding, does not
  radiate (RIEMF and pickup discipline as for the main coil, C19).
- Under radiation, the cal circuit itself is exposed: RIEMF adds an
  error current/EMF in the injection loop ([R056] mechanism; Inferred
  transfer ΓÇö flagged, risk RR-12), and insulation leakage changes the
  delivered `I_cal` unless the readback shunt sits electrically close to
  the winding (design rule: **sense at the winding, not at the source**).

### 5.4 The winding's own reference problem (stage-required; Derived)

`G_cal` is geometry + magnetics. The stage forbids assuming it stays
known, and the evidence supports the caution: **no measurement of
radiation-induced coil-constant/effective-area drift exists for any
coil** (radiation review ┬º4 gap; metrology baseline [R069], [R070]), and
thermal expansion alone changes `G_cal` at the `╬▒_thermal┬╖╬öT` level.
Consequences:

1. Only the **products** `S_H┬╖G_cal`, `K_C┬╖G_cal` are identifiable
   (CASE E). A reference-chain drift is indistinguishable from sensor
   gain drift *within the winding system alone*.
2. The JET RHP record shows the strength and the limit of the same-die
   approach: 11.5 years, SD Γëê 0.07 % sensitivity stability across
   >19,000 pulses including D-T ([H003], [H007], C05) ΓÇö but a co-located
   same-technology reference cannot by construction detect common-mode
   (shared radiation/thermal) drift of die and winding together (C05
   limitation). Mechanism diversity (geometric constant vs semiconductor
   transport) makes common-mode drift *physically unlikely* but not
   logically excluded (Inferred, stage-20 ┬º5.5).
3. **Resolution in this architecture: triangulation, not trust.** The
   winding is itself referenced against the machine-model anchor at
   every vacuum-shot epoch (CASE D identifies `S_H` and `K_C`
   absolutely; combined with the lock-in products this *solves for
   `G_cal` at each anchor epoch* ΓÇö Derived). Between anchors, `G_cal`
   drift is bounded by the closure test below, and its residual drift
   rate enters the uncertainty budget explicitly (┬º6.3) rather than
   being assumed zero.

### 5.5 Triangle-closure consistency test (Derived; added design feature)

The three continuously-available quantities

```text
╧ü_HC   = S_H/K_C            (ambient AC cross-regression, CASE A invariant)
╧Ç_H    = S_H┬╖G_cal          (Hall-side lock-in)
╧Ç_C    = K_C┬╖G_cal          (coil-side lock-in)
```

satisfy the identity `╧Ç_H / ╧Ç_C Γëí ╧ü_HC` for all t. The **closure
residual** `╬╡_╬ö = ╧Ç_H/╧Ç_C ΓêÆ ╧ü_HC` is measurable continuously and must be
zero to within noise regardless of drift in any single quantity.
`╬╡_╬ö Γëá 0` indicts the *measurement paths* (demodulator fault, spectral
collision, coil nonlinearity at `f_inj`, injection-line contamination) ΓÇö
a fault-detection channel that costs nothing extra. Note what it cannot
do: closure holds identically under any {`S_H`, `K_C`, `G_cal`} drift,
so it provides **no drift attribution** ΓÇö it validates the
instrumentation, not the calibration (consistent with Theorem 1; no
free lunch).

## 6. Estimator and compensation logic

### 6.1 Estimator states and structure

**Proposed** (structure per stage-20 estimator-requirements rows;
augmented-bias-state precedent [H015], [H004]):

- **Core filter (always on):** states
  `x = [B, x_I, b_H, b_C (or m), ╧ä_L]`, with `S_H, K_C` held at their
  last anchored values between epochs; random-walk/OU priors band-limited
  below `╧ë_d`; innovation ╧ç┬▓ monitored per channel.
- **Gain-tracking layer (HA):** lock-in outputs `╧Ç_H, ╧Ç_C` as auxiliary
  measurements updating slowly-varying multiplicative states
  `s_H = S_H/S_H^anchor`, `k_C = K_C/K_C^anchor`; the filter treats them
  as direct (noisy) observations of the relative gains, valid under the
  ┬º5.2 orthogonality condition.
- **Anchor-epoch processors (scheduled):** vacuum-shot least squares on
  `[B_ref, 1]` and `[ß╕é_ref, 1]` (CASE D); zero-field offset reads
  (CASE C2); repeated-waveform ratio regression (CASE 6). Each epoch
  writes `{┼£_H, K╠é_C, b╠é_H, b╠é_C, ─£_cal, cov}` to the calibration ledger
  (S5) with full uncertainty.
- **Fault bank (always on):** ╧ü-jump alarm; triangle-closure residual;
  innovation ╧ç┬▓; GLR change-point tests on gain states;
  loss-of-injection detector; (top tier) three-channel voting per
  CASE G / confounding test 6. Abrupt-vs-slow signatures are used as a
  *heuristic prior* for failure-vs-drift sorting, never as proof
  (stage-20 confounding row 6).
- **Honesty constraint (binding):** in any regime where stage 20 proves
  non-identifiability (CASE A between anchors, CASE F quasi-static

  states and inflate reported uncertainty, not "converge" on its prior

  simulation plan (test T-NI).

### 6.2 Four compensation modes (stage-required distinction)

| Mode | Mechanism | Timing | What it corrects | Identifiability basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Online compensation** | core KF (integrator drift, offsets vs anchors); lock-in gain tracking; ╧ü-alarm-gated deweighting | continuous | `x_I, m, ╧ä_L, b_C`; relative `S_H, K_C` (HA); field estimate fusion | C02 direction (CASE C2/I); CASE E products; CASE A invariant |

| **Fault detection** | fault bank S4 (╧ç┬▓, ╧ü-jump, GLR, closure, loss-of-injection, voting) | continuous | nothing ΓÇö it *flags*; triggers deweighting, early anchor, or channel exclusion | detection Γëá attribution (confounding 6); attribution only with diversity (CASE G) |

### 6.3 Uncertainty propagation (Derived budgets)

Every reported field value carries a variance composed of:

1. **Anchor chain:** vacuum-model error `╬┤B_ref/B_ref` maps 1:1 into

   current-log accuracy; timing skew into `ß╕é_ref`.
2. **Between-anchor drift:** random-walk growth of frozen states ΓÇö
   `var(S_H)` grows as `q_S┬╖(tΓêÆt_anchor)` with `q_S` set from measured
   drift statistics (bench Tier 1 first, updated by rung-5 data);
   reported, never hidden. This is where Theorem 1's common-mode
   blindness lives in the numbers.
3. **Gain-tracking noise:** lock-in variance (┬º5.2 formula) plus `G_cal`
   drift-rate allowance (┬º5.4.3).
4. **Coil-as-reference term (case 2 use):** coil-chain bias `╬┤(╬öB)`
   enters `╬┤S_H/S_H Γëê ΓêÆ╬┤(╬öB)/╬öB` multiplicatively; integrator noise
   makes coil-derived `╬öB` a random walk, bounding usable regression
   windows (stage-20 ┬º5.2).
5. **Environmental attribution:** temperature-coefficient uncertainty ├ù
   ╬öT excursion; TΓÇôD collinearity penalty when histories correlate
   (CASE J: attribution variance ΓåÆ Γê₧ as correlation ΓåÆ 1 ΓÇö reported as a
   conditioning number, not silently regularized).
6. **Dosimetry (campaign):** foil C/E = 1.05 ┬▒ 0.13 class uncertainty
   (C26) on the fluence axis; surrogate-to-target flux-gap factor stated
   whenever screening data is extrapolated ([R073], [R074]).

Accuracy claims in this architecture are therefore always of the form
"X % relative to the anchor epoch, growing at the stated rate between
anchors" ΓÇö no unconditional absolute-accuracy number is claimable, by
Theorem 1 (Derived).

---

## 7. Radiation mechanisms: in-situ measurable vs ex-situ (stage-required)

| Mechanism / quantity | In-situ measurable? | How / why not | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Relative Hall gain drift `S_H(t)/S_H(t_0)` | **Yes** (HA) | lock-in products; anchor ratios; repeated waveform | CASE E/6; C11 precedent [H059] |
| Absolute `S_H` | **Per-epoch only** | vacuum-shot anchor (machine off-plasma) | CASE D; [P013] |
| Hall offset drift `b_H` | **Per-epoch only** | zero-field epochs; structurally invisible to AC injection | Theorem 1; C07 |
| Hall resistance `R_H` (carrier removal / mobility proxy) | **Yes** | 4-wire bias telemetry; no field reference needed | Derived; mechanism per [R003], [R043] |
| Hall noise spectrum change | **Yes** | quiescent-period PSD monitoring | Derived (monitoring practice) |
| Coil/integrator additive drift (`b_C`, `m`, RIEMF) | **Yes** (given Hall anchor + dB/dt variation) | the C02 hardware-proven direction; zero-dB/dt segments read `b_C` directly | [H004], [H005], C19 |
| Coil gain `K_C` / effective-area drift | **Partially** | `╧Ç_C` product + anchor epochs; no in-situ separation of `A_eff` from readout gain | CASE E/D; gap: no dose-to-area data ([R069], [R070] note) |
| Which channel drifted (attribution) | **Only with diversity** | three-channel voting + measured T + decorrelated histories | CASE G/J; C18, C21 |
| Temperature-vs-dose split of a drift | **Conditionally** | measured T + pre-characterized `╬▒_S` + engineered decorrelation | CASE J; C22 hysteresis limit |
| Fluence/spectrum at the head | **Integrating in situ, read ex situ** | activation foils: retrieved and counted after exposure; online per-species spectrometry at the head is not in the evidence base (Unknown) | C26, [R072]ΓÇô[R076] |
| Mobility vs carrier-density decomposition of a gain drift | **No** | requires van der Pauw / Hall-bar lab measurement | [R003] method |
| Transmutation dopant identification | **No** | materials analysis (post-exposure) | [R025], [R001], C24 |
| Deep-level/trap characterization | **No** | DLTS-class lab work | radiation review ┬º1 |
| Annealing recovery curves | **No** (requires controlled T-history) | furnace/ramp protocols post-exposure | [R024], C22 |
| Insulation resistance / interlaminar integrity | **No** (dedicated test) | megger/mechanical test at maintenance | [R061], [R062], [R068] |
| Readout SET rate | **Yes** (detection) | fault bank catches ms-scale transients; correction is exclusion, not calibration | [R052], C25 |

---

## 8. Cross-sensitivity, common-mode failure, reference degradation

- **Cross-axis response:** single-axis analysis assumed (stage-20 ┬º2.4);
  misalignment inseparable from gain with a single-axis reference ΓÇö
  budgeted (┬º6.3.1); bench characterization required (Tier 1);
  vertical-Hall cross-sensitivity evidence [H047].
- **Temperature cross-sensitivity:** first-class state; the J-corr
  failure (T Γê¥ D ΓåÆ rank 1) is a *scheduling* problem ΓÇö engineered thermal
  excursions decorrelated from fluence accumulation are part of the
  campaign design, not an afterthought (CASE J-decorr).
- **Common-mode failure classes and their only countermeasures:**
  (i) Hall+coil common gain shift ΓÇö invisible in-pair (Theorem 1);
  countered only by anchor cadence (C) and mechanism diversity (D);
  (ii) die+winding common shift ΓÇö invisible to self-test (C05);
  countered by the machine-model anchor;
  (iii) whole-head common environment (T excursion, flux transient) ΓÇö
  countered by telemetry (T, `R_H`) and post-hoc reprocessing;
  (iv) shared-electronics events (SETs, rail glitches) ΓÇö countered by
  fault bank + channel-level electrical separation (block design ┬º4.3).
- **Reference degradation:** every reference in this architecture is
  assigned a *degradation observable*: `G_cal` ΓåÆ closure + anchor solve
  (┬º5.4ΓÇô5.5); machine-current model ΓåÆ vacuum-shot residuals vs model
  ([P013]-class verification); metallic-Hall witness ΓåÆ its own `R` and
  noise telemetry + ratio consistency (single-source basis flagged,
  C18); zero-field epochs ΓåÆ ambient-field audit (risk RR-24); dosimetry
  ΓåÆ C/E protocol (C26). A reference with no degradation observable is
  not admitted into the estimator (design rule, Derived from stage-20
  ┬º4 feasibility-matrix reading).

---

## 9. Accuracy/cost drivers and budget tiers

No vendor prices are quoted anywhere (none are in the evidence base);
cost classes are order-of-magnitude *labels* (labeled estimate) tied to
`DECISION_FRAMEWORK.md`'s tier structure. Stop/go gates G0ΓÇôG6 are defined
in the validation plan ┬º10 and summarized here.

| Tier | Content | Dominant accuracy drivers | Dominant cost drivers | Entry gate | Exit (go) gate | Stop rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T0 ΓÇö simulation** | reusable package per validation plan; synthetic fault injection | model fidelity to ┬º2 parameterization; honesty test T-NI | engineering time only | ΓÇö | **G0:** estimator meets metric targets on identifiable scenarios AND correctly reports non-identifiability on CASE-A/F scenarios | if targets unreachable even with perfect references ΓåÆ redesign before any hardware spend |
| **T1 ΓÇö bench truth (MVD hardware)** | existing Hall + wound coil + precision current source/Helmholtz + temperature control; traceable transfer standard | reference traceability; temperature-coefficient characterization; noise floors; alignment | bench components; transfer-standard access; time | G0 pass | **G1:** anchored-hybrid calibration repeatable across ΓëÑ3 cycles within the T0-predicted uncertainty; `╬▒_S, ╬▓_b` characterized | if bench repeatability Γë½ prediction and cause not found ΓåÆ architecture assumptions wrong; halt and diagnose |
| **T2 ΓÇö self-test hybrid (HA hardware)** | + cal winding, traceable current ref, dual lock-in, drift emulation, long-duration soak | `G_cal` characterization; heating ceiling (┬º5.3); spectral survey quality; emulated-drift recovery accuracy | winding fabrication/characterization; reference electronics; long-run test time | G1 pass | **G2/G3:** emulated gain/offset drifts recovered within CI; closure residual stable over ΓëÑ multi-day soak; drift-attribution logic validated on emulated faults | if injected-reference stability cannot beat the drift resolution target ΓåÆ Option B layer is not earning its complexity; descope to MVD (C-only anchoring) |
| **T3 ΓÇö environmental qualification (collaborator-led)** | material screening ΓåÆ neutron/gamma qualification with dosimetry, material diversity, pre/post + in-situ protocol per FOCS/foil templates (C20/C26) | species/spectrum match to target environment (C12/C16); dosimetry C/E; sample size; T control during exposure | facility access (never assumed ΓÇö no facility commitment exists in this plan); collaborator effort; activated-hardware logistics | G3 pass + collaborator agreement | **G4/G5:** screening quantifies `f_S,s` with stated uncertainty; qualification confirms compensation closes the loop at target accuracy | if screening shows drift below the in-situ method's detection floor ΓåÆ in-situ recal is unnecessary (simplify to MVD + scheduled recal: a *good* outcome); if drift is large, non-monotonic, and unattributable ΓåÆ hybrid compensation is falsified for that material; pivot to Option D/F material change |

(Four tiers ΓëÑ the required three; T0 costs no hardware and is the
mandatory first spend.)

### 9.4 HSX-paper decoupling (binding statement)

Tiers T0ΓÇôT2 and gates G0ΓÇôG3 involve **no radiation exposure of any
kind** and constitute the complete architecture-validation content
relevant to the user's current first-author HSX trajectory. T3 exists
only as a collaborator-led, later or coauthored work package
(per `MISSION.md` boundary and root scope rule); no output of T0ΓÇôT2, and
no HSX deliverable, depends on T3 occurring. Radiation results may be
*cited as complementary or outlook* in first-author work, never claimed
experimentally (root `CLAUDE.md` scope rule).

---

## 10. Unresolved engineering risks (summary)

Full register with likelihood/impact/mitigation:
`outputs\03_RADIATION_RISK_REGISTER.csv` (24 rows, RR-01ΓÇªRR-24). The five
that most threaten the architecture (Derived ranking by
impact ├ù irreducibility):

1. **RR-01/RR-02 ΓÇö GaN drift magnitude unknown (C14):** every cadence,
   window, and threshold in ┬º5ΓÇô6 is sized provisionally until rung-5
   screening data exists; the architecture is designed to *measure* its
   way out of this, but cannot be proven sufficient before that data.
2. **RR-13 ΓÇö common-mode blindness between anchors (Theorem 1):**
   irreducible in-pair; bounded only by anchor cadence and (top tier)
   diversity; the residual is an honest uncertainty term, not a solved
   problem.
3. **RR-12/RR-08 ΓÇö reference-chain drift under radiation (`G_cal`,
   `A_eff`):** zero direct evidence either way (no dose-to-geometry
   measurements exist); triangulation bounds but does not eliminate it.
4. **RR-18 ΓÇö witness-channel single-source basis ([R071], C18):** the
   attribution tier rests on an unreplicated null result.
5. **RR-16/RR-17 ΓÇö planning-level extrapolation traps (C16, C17):** any
   shortcut that sizes the design from proton or single-species data
   risks the documented ~14├ù class of error; enforced by the
   species-indexing discipline of ┬º2.

---

## 11. Consistency statement

Checked line-by-line against stage 20: every "covers" claim in ┬º3ΓÇô┬º7
cites the enabling CASE and inherits its conditions; no claim exceeds the
feasibility matrix (`02_MUTUAL_CALIBRATION_FEASIBILITY.md` ┬º2); the
estimator is required to refuse convergence where stage 20 proves
non-identifiability (┬º6.1). No statement in this file asserts that any
radiation experiment has been performed by the user or is required for
the user's current first-author work. Simulation is never called
validation; [R050]-class simulation-only sources are not cited as
experimental anywhere in this file.

# 03 ΓÇö Simulation and validation plan

Stage 30 (`30_radiation_compensation`). Produced and signed off by Fable 5
(xhigh). Source/claim IDs cite `outputs\01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv` /
`outputs\01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv`; stage-20 CASE references cite
`outputs\02_OBSERVABILITY_AND_IDENTIFIABILITY.md`. Architecture context:
`outputs\03_RADIATION_COMPENSATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` (cited as ARCH ┬ºx).
Labels: **Observed / Derived / Inferred / Proposed / Unknown**.

---

## 1. Purpose and evidence-class boundary (binding)

This plan specifies (a) a simulation package precise enough for a later
implementer to build **without inventing any scientific model content**,
and (b) the staged experimental ladder that can falsify the ARCH concept
at the lowest possible cost.

**Three evidence classes are never mixed (per `CLAUDE.md` and
`SOURCE_POLICY.md`):**

| Class | What it can establish | What it can never establish |
|---|---|---|
| **Simulated** (rungs 1) | estimator correctness, structural identifiability behavior, fault-logic coverage, uncertainty-propagation correctness | any device physics; any drift magnitude; any claim of "validation" of the concept against reality |
| **Bench** (rungs 2ΓÇô4) | non-radiation identifiability conditions in hardware; noise floors; temperature coefficients; reference traceability; emulated-drift recovery | radiation response of anything |
| **Radiation** (rungs 5ΓÇô6, collaborator-led) | species/spectrum-specific drift magnitudes `f_S,s`, `f_b,s`; compensation closure under real damage | nothing about species/spectra not actually used (C16: cross-species scaling can err ~14├ù; C17: mixed fields non-additive) |

Simulation results are always reported as "synthetic"; the phrase
"experimental validation" is reserved for rungs 2+ hardware results.
Rungs 5ΓÇô7 are outside the user's current first-author HSX scope
(ARCH ┬º9.4; `00_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md` C6).

---

## 2. State-space specification

**Proposed** (implements ARCH ┬º2 exactly; a coder implements these
equations verbatim ΓÇö no scientific choices are left open, only numerical
ones).

### 2.1 Continuous-time truth model

States `x`, inputs `u`, outputs `y`:

```text
Field:        B(t)                          [T]   (scenario-defined input trajectory)
Injection:    B_inj(t) = G_cal(t)┬╖I_cal(t)  [T]   (u: I_cal; state: G_cal)
Integrator:   dx_I/dt = ΓêÆx_I/╧ä_L + g┬╖d(B+B_inj)/dt + m(t)

Hall gain:    S_H(t) = S_H0┬╖[1 + ╬▒_S┬╖╬öT(t) + f_S(╬ª(t)) + h_S(a(t))] ┬╖ (1 + w_S(t))
Hall offset:  b_H(t) = b_H0 + ╬▓_b┬╖╬öT(t) + f_b(╬ª(t)) + h_b(a(t)) + w_b(t)
Coil gain:    K_C(t) = K_C0┬╖[1 + ╬▒_K┬╖╬öT(t) + f_K(╬ª(t))] ┬╖ (1 + w_K(t))
Coil offset:  b_C(t) = b_C0 + ╬▓_c┬╖╬öT(t) + r_RIEMF┬╖╧å╠ç(t) + w_c(t)
Cal transfer: G_cal(t) = G_cal0┬╖[1 + ╬▒_G┬╖╬öT(t) + f_G(╬ª(t))] ┬╖ (1 + w_G(t))
Drift rate:   m(t)   = m0 + w_m(t)
Annealing:    da/dt  = ΓêÆa/╧ä_a(T) + ╬║(T)┬╖d╬ª_ann/dt        (hysteresis state; see 2.4)

Outputs:
  y_H = S_H┬╖(B + B_inj) + b_H + n_H                      [V]
  y_C = K_C┬╖(h_C Γêù d(B+B_inj)/dt) + b_C + n_C            [V]  (direct mode)
  y_I = x_I + n_I                                        [V]  (integrated mode)
  y_T = T + n_T                                          [K]
  y_R = R_H(t) + n_R                                     [╬⌐]  (R_H = R_H0┬╖[1 + ╬│_R┬╖╬öT + f_R(╬ª)])
  y_D = ╬ª(t_read) ┬╖ (1 + n_D)                            (fluence, read only at retrieval epochs ΓÇö foils, C26)
```

`h_C` is a first-order low-pass with pole `╧ë_C` plus pure delay `╬┤t_C`;
the Hall channel optionally gets pole `a_H` and delay `╬┤t_H` (case-9
scenarios). All `w_ΓÇó(t)` are independent random walks or OU processes
with intensities `q_ΓÇó` (config); all `n_ΓÇó` are white Gaussian with
variances `╧â_ΓÇó┬▓` (config). Species indexing: `╬ª` is a **vector** over
species s; every `f_ΓÇó` takes the vector and applies per-species curves ΓÇö
the package must refuse a scalar-fluence config when more than one
species is nonzero (enforces C16/C17 discipline programmatically).

### 2.2 Radiation response functions `f_ΓÇó(╬ª)` ΓÇö placeholder policy (binding)

**No GaN/AlGaN Hall-plate neutron response exists (C14).** The package
therefore ships with *labeled placeholder families*, never presented as
device predictions:

- `f = 0` (null case);
- linear `f = cΓéü┬╖╬ª_s`;
- saturating `f = c_sat┬╖(1 ΓêÆ exp(ΓêÆ╬ª_s/╬ª_0))` ΓÇö the bounded-asymptote
  *hypothesis* (Inferred, C23, proton-only basis [R036]ΓÇô[R038]);
- piecewise/two-regime (TID-like, C22 basis [R024]);
- user-supplied tabulated curve (the rung-5 output slot).

Config files must carry a `basis` field per curve:
`{placeholder | literature:<source_id> | measured:<dataset_id>}`. Any
figure or report generated from `placeholder` curves must carry a
"synthetic placeholder ΓÇö no device basis" watermark string. (Derived
requirement from the C14 gap; prevents the simulation from silently
becoming fake device evidence.)

### 2.3 Discretization and estimator-side model

Truth model integrated at `dt_sim`; measurements sampled at `dt_H`,
`dt_C` (allowing inter-channel skew `╬┤t` injection). The estimator (ARCH
┬º6.1) uses the *same equations* with states
`[B, x_I, b_H, b_C|m, ╧ä_L, s_H, k_C]` and treats anchors/lock-in outputs
as scheduled measurements. Estimator-model mismatch scenarios (S9) use a
deliberately reduced estimator model against the full truth model.

### 2.4 Annealing/hysteresis state

`a(t)` accumulates during exposure and relaxes with
temperature-dependent `╧ä_a(T)`; recovery fraction capped (`h_S` recovers
only a configurable share, transmutation share non-recoverable ΓÇö
structure per C22/C24 evidence; all rate constants are placeholders per
┬º2.2 policy). Purpose: reproduce the CASE J window-validity problem so
the estimator's windowed attribution logic can be tested ΓÇö not to
predict any real device.

---

## 3. Parameter schema

**Proposed** config schema (one namespace per block; YAML/JSON; all
fields required, units in-name):

```text
hall:      S_H0_V_per_T, b_H0_V, R_H0_ohm, alpha_S_per_K, beta_b_V_per_K,
           gamma_R_per_K, sigma_H_V, q_S, q_b, pole_a_H_rad_s|null,
           delay_s, f_S{basis,type,params[per species]}, f_b{...}, f_R{...},
           anneal{tau_a_s(T)_params, kappa_params, recoverable_fraction}
coil:      K_C0_Vs_per_T, b_C0_V, alpha_K_per_K, beta_c_V_per_K,
           sigma_C_V, q_K, q_c, pole_w_C_rad_s, delay_s,
           riemf_r_V_per_flux_rate|0, f_K{...}
integ:     g, m0_V_per_s, tau_L_s, x_I0_V, sigma_I_V, q_m
calwind:   G_cal0_T_per_A, alpha_G_per_K, q_G, f_G{...},
           R_cal_ohm, R_th_K_per_W        (heating model, ARCH ┬º5.3)
inject:    waveform{sine|toggle|prbs|off}, f_inj_Hz, I_amp_A, T_int_s,
           schedule
env:       T_profile, Phi_profiles[per species], dose_rate_profiles,
           correlation_controls (for CASE J scenarios)
refs:      machine_anchor{schedule, dB_levels_T[>=2], dBdt_values[>=2],
           ref_error_rel, position_error, timing_skew_s},
           zero_field{schedule, ambient_residual_T},
           bench_absolute{uncertainty_rel},
           dosimetry{CoverE_mean=1.05, CoverE_sd=0.13 basis C26, read_epochs}
sim:       dt_sim_s, dt_H_s, dt_C_s, skew_s, duration_s, seed, solver
estimator: variant{MVD|HA|HA+witness}, q_priors, freeze_policy,
           fault_thresholds
```

Defaults ship as `placeholder` basis; nothing in the schema encodes a
claimed GaN number. Bench-measured values (rung 2+) enter as
`measured:<dataset_id>` with the dataset archived beside the config.

---

## 4. Scenario matrix

Each scenario states its stage-20 anchor so expected estimator behavior
is pre-registered (Derived from stage 20, not tuned after the fact):

| ID | Scenario | Truth setup | Pre-registered expected behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Unreferenced pair, everything drifting | no anchors, no injection | CASE A: estimator must freeze gains/offsets, report ╧ü only; honesty test T-NI applies |
| S2 | Vacuum-shot anchoring cycle | machine anchor per schedule, ΓëÑ2 levels + ramp/flat-top | CASE D: all four parameters recovered within CRLB-class bounds at each epoch |
| S3 | Quasi-static flat-top, no injection | dB/dt Γëê 0 window | CASE F: uncertainty growth exactly as budgeted; no spurious convergence |
| S4 | Quasi-static + injection ON | S3 + spectrally clean tone | CASE E: gain products tracked through flat-top; b_H untouched (stays frozen) |
| S5 | Spectral collision | ambient line at/near f_inj | CASE E-collide: collision detector fires; gain tracking deweighted, not corrupted |
| S6 | Radiation drift ramp, T decorrelated | f_S ramp (placeholder curve), independent T excursions | CASE J-decorr: attribution splits kT vs kD within CI |
| S7 | Radiation drift ramp, T Γê¥ ╬ª | correlated histories | CASE J-corr: attribution reports conditioning failure (no silent split) |
| S8 | Common-mode gain event | S_H and K_C shifted together between anchors | Theorem 1: NO in-pair alarm expected; next anchor epoch must catch and re-anchor; report flags the blind interval |
| S9 | Model mismatch | truth has pole/delay/nonlinearity absent from estimator model | residual/╧ç┬▓ flags; no false drift attribution (confounding 6 heuristic only) |
| S10 | Annealing window | exposure stop ΓåÆ recovery with T history | windowed attribution validity enforced (C22-driven logic) |
| S11 | Integrator-only stress | m, ╧ä_L drift, constant-ramp segments | CASE I vs I-ramp: g┬╖r+m confound reproduced and resolved only when dB/dt varies |
| S12 | Long-duration soak (synthetic twin of rung 4) | slow drifts everywhere, realistic anchor cadence | end-to-end uncertainty budget matches ensemble truth-error statistics |

## 5. Fault-injection catalog

Injectable at configurable onset/magnitude/shape (step, ramp, sag,
burst):

F1 Hall gain step/ramp; F2 Hall offset step/ramp; F3 coil gain
step/ramp; F4 integrator drift-rate step; F5 integrator leak change;
F6 common-mode Hall+coil gain shift (Theorem-1 probe); F7 cal-chain
drift `G_cal` (reference degradation, ARCH ┬º5.4); F8 loss/partial loss
of injection current; F9 RIEMF ramp on `b_C` (flux-rate-correlated);
F10 SET-like ms transients on either channel ([R052] class); F11
saturation/clipping of coil readout (case 9); F12 timing-skew step;
F13 zero-field-epoch contamination (ambient residual Γëá 0, RR-24);
F14 witness-channel failure (top tier: voting must not be fooled).

Every fault has a pre-registered expected detector response
(which alarm, max latency class, and what must NOT fire ΓÇö false-
attribution guards). Coverage matrix (fault ├ù detector) is a shipped
test artifact.

---

## 6. Reference datasets

1. **Synthetic truth sets:** generated by the package itself with pinned
   seeds/configs (one per scenario S1ΓÇôS12); archived as
   `datasets\synthetic\<scenario>_<config_hash>`.
2. **Bench datasets (rungs 2ΓÇô4 outputs):** schema-defined slots
   (`measured:<dataset_id>`) ΓÇö raw channel streams + reference logs +
   environment telemetry + calibration-ledger entries. None exist yet;
   the package must run fully without them (Unknown until rung 2).
3. **Machine waveform templates:** field/current waveform *shapes* may
   be drawn from the folder-07 HSX shot archive (coil-current logs) as
   scenario inputs, clearly labeled as waveform templates ΓÇö never as
   sensor-truth data (the 07 folder is read-only context; no value from
   it becomes a claimed measurement of this architecture).
4. **No fabricated data:** the package contains no dataset presented as
   a device measurement; placeholder-basis outputs carry the ┬º2.2
   watermark. (Binding.)

---

## 7. Metrics

| ID | Metric | Definition | Used at |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Field accuracy | RMSE and max-error of `B╠é` vs truth, absolute and relative-to-anchor | S2ΓÇôS12, G0/G1 |
| M2 | Parameter recovery | bias and variance of each parameter estimate vs truth; ratio to CRLB from the stage-20 FIM machinery | S2, S4, S6, S11 |
| M3 | Coverage honesty | fraction of time truth lies inside reported 1╧â/2╧â intervals (target: nominal within stated tolerance) ΓÇö the headline honesty metric | all scenarios |
| M4 | Detection performance | per-fault detection latency and missed-detection rate at fixed false-alarm budget (ARL-style) | F1ΓÇôF14 |
| M5 | Attribution accuracy | confusion matrix over {Hall gain, Hall offset, coil gain, integrator, reference-chain, common-mode/none} | S6ΓÇôS9, F-catalog |
| M6 | Non-identifiability honesty (T-NI) | in S1/S3/S8 blind intervals: estimator must NOT reduce reported variance below the open-loop growth curve; any "convergence" in a proven-unidentifiable direction = FAIL | S1, S3, S8 |
| M7 | Closure residual behavior | ╬╡_╬ö (ARCH ┬º5.5) null under drift, non-null under path faults F7/F8/F11 | S4ΓÇôS5, F7/F8/F11 |
| M8 | Budget fidelity | end-to-end reported uncertainty vs ensemble truth error over ΓëÑ100-seed Monte Carlo | S12, G0 |

## 8. Test suite

- **Unit:** each model equation vs closed-form solutions (integrator
  response, lock-in output for known tone, annealing relaxation);
  schema validation (species-vector enforcement; basis-field
  enforcement).
- **Regression:** reproduce stage-20 rank results by running
  `tools\observability_rank_tests.py` (kept reusable at stage 20)
  against the package's Jacobians ΓÇö CASE A/B/C1/C2/D/D-flat/E/
  E-collide/F/G/H/I/I-ramp/J must match rank-for-rank. This binds the
  package to the proven structure (no silent model drift).
- **Acceptance:** scenario matrix S1ΓÇôS12 with pre-registered behaviors;
  fault coverage matrix; M3/M6 honesty gates. A run report is generated
  per config hash.
- **Estimator-abuse tests:** deliberately mis-specified priors must not
  produce confident wrong answers in unidentifiable directions (extends
  T-NI).

## 9. Reproducibility

Pinned dependencies; single-command run per scenario; every artifact
tagged with `config_hash` + seed; deterministic solvers (fixed-step for
truth model); all randomness via one seeded generator; CI-style script
that re-runs unit+regression suites; outputs include the exact config
copy. No wall-clock or machine-dependent values enter results.

---

## 10. Staged experimental ladder (rungs, gates, stop rules)

substitution); dosimetry per the validated foil protocol
(reference-field calibration ΓåÆ in-situ foils; C/E = 1.05 ┬▒ 0.13 class,

state recorded (`SOURCE_POLICY.md`); pre/post van der Pauw
decomposition (mobility vs carrier density, [R003] method); control
(unirradiated) devices held back. Sample size: ΓëÑ5 irradiated + ΓëÑ3
control devices per material/condition (Proposed; scale consistent with
the 9-sample InSb campaign [R003] ΓÇö defensible as a minimum for a mean
drift curve with outlier rejection, not for population statistics).

`measured:` curves. Stop rules (either direction is decisive):
drift below in-situ detection floor ΓåÆ in-situ recal unnecessary,
simplify architecture (good outcome); drift large/non-monotonic/
unattributable ΓåÆ hybrid compensation falsified for that material;
pivot per ARCH ┬º9 T3 stop rule.

dosimetry) under representative exposure with in-situ anchors per the

dataset in the ledger, C20: continuous cross-validation against an
independent reference, pre/post baselines). Acceptance: in-situ
compensation closes to the target accuracy against the independent
reference; every ┬º7 in-situ claim of the ARCH table demonstrated or
amended. No facility, schedule, or access is assumed to exist ΓÇö
this rung is a specification for a future collaboration agreement.

can demonstrate on a stellarator/tokamak vacuum+plasma cycle
independently of rungs 5ΓÇô6 ΓÇö anchoring, offset epochs, integrator

demonstration only after rung 6. Sequencing decisions belong to stage 60.

mandatory reporting format from rung 2 onward (reference chain,
between-anchor growth, tracking noise, environmental attribution,
dosimetry where applicable).

**Proposed module boundary (implements, never re-derives, the science):**

```text
model/      truth-model integrator (┬º2 equations, config-driven)
schema/     config schema + validators (┬º3; species/basis enforcement)
estimator/  KF core, lock-in, anchor processors, fault bank (ARCH ┬º6.1)
faults/     injection catalog (┬º5)
```

   source ([R067]) ΓÇö treated as unknown, not modeled.
5. Rungs 5ΓÇô7 assume no specific facility, price, or schedule; none is
   claimed to exist.

"""Stage-30 output validator (reusable; mirrors tools/validate_10d_outputs.py).

Checks:
  1. All three stage-30 outputs exist and are nontrivial.
  2. Risk register parses, has the exact required header, unique risk_ids.
  3. Every evidence_id in the register resolves to a ledger source_id or an
     evidence-map claim_id.
  4. Every bracketed [Hxxx]/[Rxxx]/[Pxxx] source ID and every Cxx claim ID
     cited in the two stage-30 markdown files resolves likewise.
  5. Register enumerations (likelihood/impact/decision_gate) use the allowed
     vocabularies.
"""
import csv
import os
import re
import sys

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT = os.path.join(BASE, "outputs")

REQUIRED_HEADER = [
    "risk_id", "component", "mechanism", "radiation_or_environment",
    "observable_effect", "detectability", "compensation_possible",
    "reference_required", "likelihood", "impact", "evidence_ids",
    "mitigation", "validation_test", "residual_risk", "decision_gate",
]

FILES = {
    "arch": os.path.join(OUT, "03_RADIATION_COMPENSATION_ARCHITECTURE.md"),
    "plan": os.path.join(OUT, "03_SIMULATION_AND_VALIDATION_PLAN.md"),
    "risk": os.path.join(OUT, "03_RADIATION_RISK_REGISTER.csv"),
}

LIKELIHOOD_VOCAB_PREFIX = ("low", "medium", "high", "unknown")
IMPACT_VOCAB_PREFIX = ("low", "medium", "high", "unknown")
GATE_RE = re.compile(r"^G[0-7]$")

failures = []
checks = 0


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    global checks
    checks += 1
    status = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"[{status}] {name}" + (f" ΓÇö {detail}" if detail else ""))
    if not ok:
        failures.append(name)


def load_valid_ids():
    ids = set()
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            ids.add(row["source_id"].strip())
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            ids.add(row["claim_id"].strip())
    return ids


def main():
    valid_ids = load_valid_ids()
    print(f"loaded {len(valid_ids)} valid source+claim IDs")

    # 1. existence / nontriviality
    for key, path in FILES.items():
        exists = os.path.isfile(path)
        size = os.path.getsize(path) if exists else 0
        check(f"{key} exists and nontrivial", exists and size > 2000,
              f"{os.path.basename(path)} size={size}")

    # 2. register parse + header + uniqueness
    with open(FILES["risk"], encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        reader = csv.reader(f)
        header = next(reader)
        rows = list(reader)
    check("register header exact", header == REQUIRED_HEADER,
          "match" if header == REQUIRED_HEADER else f"got {header}")
    check("register row count", len(rows) >= 15, f"{len(rows)} rows")
    ids = [r[0] for r in rows]
    check("risk_id unique", len(ids) == len(set(ids)))
    check("all rows full-width", all(len(r) == len(REQUIRED_HEADER) for r in rows))

    # 3. evidence_ids resolve
    idx = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("evidence_ids")
    bad = []
    for r in rows:
        for eid in r[idx].split(";"):
            eid = eid.strip()
            if eid and eid not in valid_ids:
                bad.append((r[0], eid))
    check("register evidence_ids resolve", not bad, f"unresolved: {bad}" if bad else "all resolve")

    # 4. enum vocab + gates
    li = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("likelihood")
    im = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("impact")
    dg = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("decision_gate")
    bad_enum = [r[0] for r in rows
                if not r[li].startswith(LIKELIHOOD_VOCAB_PREFIX)
                or not r[im].startswith(IMPACT_VOCAB_PREFIX)
                or not GATE_RE.match(r[dg])]
    check("register enums/gates valid", not bad_enum, str(bad_enum) if bad_enum else "ok")

    # 5. markdown citations resolve
    id_re = re.compile(r"\[([HRP]\d{3})\]")
    claim_re = re.compile(r"\bC\d{2}\b")
    for key in ("arch", "plan"):
        text = open(FILES[key], encoding="utf-8").read()
        cited = set(id_re.findall(text))
        claims = set(c for c in claim_re.findall(text))
        bad_src = sorted(c for c in cited if c not in valid_ids)
        bad_claim = sorted(c for c in claims if c not in valid_ids)
        check(f"{key} source IDs resolve ({len(cited)} cited)", not bad_src,
              f"unresolved: {bad_src}" if bad_src else "all resolve")
        check(f"{key} claim IDs resolve ({len(claims)} cited)", not bad_claim,
              f"unresolved: {bad_claim}" if bad_claim else "all resolve")

    print(f"\n{checks - len(failures)}/{checks} checks passed")
    if failures:
        print("FAILURES:", failures)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## Routing rationale

| Work type | Assigned model | Effort | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inventory and traceability | Sonnet 5 | high | Mostly deterministic inspection and structured extraction |
| Hybrid and radiation search | Sonnet 5 | xhigh | Broad retrieval needs care, but evidence reconciliation is deferred |
| Applications search | Sonnet 5 | high | Wide current landscape; final priority is decided later |
| Applications/collaboration scoring | Sonnet 5 | xhigh | Substantial judgment, but bounded by the Fable-reviewed technical analysis |
| Evidence merge and all central technical decisions | Fable 5 | xhigh | Highest cost of error and strongest cross-domain reasoning need |
| Red team and final synthesis | Fable 5 | xhigh | Must challenge and sign off the full argument |

Seven of twelve stages require Fable 5 at xhigh. This satisfies the requirement
that Fable handle the most critical thinking while controlling budget on
search-heavy work.

The aliases passed to Claude Code are `sonnet` and `fable`; the installed
Claude Code version must be at least 2.1.219 so current model-category behavior
and model reporting can be checked.

## Integrity rule

For a Fable-assigned stage, the accepted final main response must report a
Fable model. Temporary main-thread adjustment followed by a Fable final result
is logged and allowed. Auxiliary/subagent use of another model is logged and
allowed. A final non-Fable or unverifiable model triggers:

1. First event: quarantine expected outputs, checkpoint all evidence, generate
   a narrowly clarified benign academic prompt, and retry once in a fresh
   Fable session with `--safe-mode`.
2. Second event: quarantine, checkpoint, stop the workflow, and require manual
   review. No silent provider or model substitution.

The retry prompt may clarify scope and remove ambiguous framing, but it may not
weaken evidence gates or change the scientific question.

`MODEL_EFFORT_LOG.csv` records requested model/effort, all reported models,
final-result integrity, session, duration, validation, and notes.

`PERFORMANCE_LOG.csv` records duration, turns, token/cache fields, reported
cost, web-search/fetch counts, final model, integrity, and current verified
source count when those fields are available in Claude's stream.
